subject: Velaris Dedicated Capacity: throughput / SLO sensitivity analysis
messages:
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@velarishealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask: baseline + peak profile for upcoming POC

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. To prepare for our POC we need a short sizing workbook that maps our usage profile to dedicated GPU counts and expected latency SLO fit. A few quick facts from our side:
- Monthly baseline: ~9M tokens/day (chat-heavy workflows)
- Typical session: ~420 tokens average (prompt + response)
- Peak pattern: 10:00–12:00 and 18:00–20:00 PDT, peak concurrency observed ~320 concurrent sessions during those windows
- Desired SLO: p95 generation latency <= 200ms (user-facing chat)

Can you provide a recommended dedicated pool (min sustained GPUs + burst) and a short sensitivity table that shows what happens if average tokens/session grows by +20% / +50%? Prefer a one-sheet we can circulate to infra/procurement.

Attached: Velaris-usage-profile.csv (hourly traces)

—Alex
Director, Product
Velaris Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@velarishealth.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask: baseline + peak profile for upcoming POC

Alex —

Thanks, this is very helpful. I ran a quick first-pass sizing and attached a working workbook (velaris_dedicated_model_v1.xlsx) that shows tokens/sec estimates, p95 SLO fit assumptions, and recommended headroom. High-level conclusions up front: 

- Sustained baseline (derived): ~104k tokens/sec sustained across 24h (9M tokens/day -> ~104k tokens/sec when smoothed to a 24h average; see sheet 'baseline').
- Peak windows: observed short-window peaks up to ~215k tokens/sec (based on your hourly traces + concurrency).
- Model assumptions: 13B dense variant (redwood-v2-13b) quantized at int8; we used conservative kernel/perf numbers from our 2027 internal perf matrix. Per A100-80GB equivalent GPU we modeled ~22k tokens/sec sustained for interactive generation at p95 <= 200ms.
- Mapping to GPUs: baseline: 5 GPUs (sustained). Peak (with 20% headroom): 11 GPUs nomimal to keep p95 under 200ms under worst-minute peaks.

Sensitivity quick-calls: +20% tokens/session -> baseline GPUs +1 (to 6), peak GPUs +2 (to 13). +50% tokens/session -> baseline +3 (to 8), peak +5 (to 16).

I'll flag that these numbers are model- and quantization-dependent (see Markus' notes below). If you agree, we can turn this into a committed dedicated offer: 6x A100-equivalent sustained with a 6-GPU burst pool for peaks, and surge credits for extreme events.

Proposed next step: quick sync Monday to run through assumptions with engineering and align on commit level.

Attachments: velaris_dedicated_model_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask: baseline + peak profile for upcoming POC

Marissa / Rohan —

Quick engineering read on the workbook. A few adjustments we should reflect in v1.1: 

1) Kernel and model variant delta
- If Velaris chooses a trimmed-redwood-13B (sparser attention variant) or uses 4-bit quantization (Q4) instead of int8, we can push sustained tokens/sec per A100 to ~28k–30k at similar p95 for short sequences (~512 tokens). That reduces GPU counts by ~20–30%.

2) Sequence length sensitivity
- The workbook assumes avg 420 tokens/session. If 90th percentile sessions are 1.5x (630 tokens) the effective tokens/sec scales linearly; we should introduce a 90th pct scenario because p95 latency is sensitive to tail session lengths.

3) Burst handling and KV cache
- For chat, prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts can reduce effective compute for subsequent tokens by ~10–15% in practice; add a 'cache' slider that reduces tokens/sec demand for sessions with repeated context.

4) Ops play: recommend a 2-GPU hot pool dedicated to sub-50ms micro-LM tasks (reranking, short completions) to keep user-facing p50s tight while the main pool handles long generations. This keeps perceived latency lower without large capacity increases.

I'll drop a v1.1 workbook with two model/quantization branches (int8 vs q4) and a 90th pct length sheet.

—Markus
Head of Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Commit framing: recommended reserved capacity tiers for Velaris (VLR-2027-045)

Team —

Based on Marissa's baseline and Markus' perf levers, here's a commercial framing we should propose to Velaris in the Monday sync: 

Option A — Conservative commit (recommended for initial POC):
- 6 A100-equivalent GPUs sustained (monthly commit), 6-GPU burst pool (on-demand)
- Includes 50 surge credits for emergency spikes (convertible to on-demand usage)
- Price: [redacted] per GPU/month; term: 3 months

Option B — Performance-optimized (saves ~20% cost if Velaris accepts Q4 quant):
- 5 A100-equivalent GPUs sustained at Q4 runtime profiles + 5-GPU burst pool
- Includes 75 surge credits
- Price: [redacted] per GPU/month; term: 6 months

Risk notes: if 90th pct length approaches +50% of avg, we should price for +30% capacity. Also confirm required p95 SLA and the allowed latency budget for reranking / tool calls.

I'll prepare a short one-pager and a DocuSign-ready letter-of-intent if the team signs off on Option A as the POC baseline.

-Neha
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@velarishealth.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask: baseline + peak profile for upcoming POC

Alex —

Thanks for the trace — we've compiled a short sensitivity pack and an initial commercial framing attached (SLA-delta-scenarios.pdf + velaris_dedicated_model_v1.xlsx). Quick summary:

- POC ask (recommended): Option A (6 sustained GPUs + 6-GPU burst, surge credits) — maps to expected baseline + safe headroom for the two daily peaks; keeps p95 generation latency ~180–200ms under modeled int8 assumptions.
- If Velaris is open to Q4 quantization and accepts the modest model-variant work, we can drop committed GPUs to 5 with similar p95s (Option B).
- Action items for Monday: 1) confirm p95 SLA target (is 200ms firm?), 2) share expected 90th pct session length, 3) decide whether we should run a quick perf run with Q4 quant on a small sample to validate the Q4 assumptions.

Can we do 30 minutes Monday 10:30 PDT to walk through the sheet and pick Option A vs B? If that works I'll circulate a short LOI and a demo checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
